### periodicPlateOptiAD2d

Identification of the two amplitudes of a body force field on a periodic plate,
with the gradient computed by forward-mode automatic differentiation (f-AD).
This is the first of three benchmarks for gradient-based optimization in linear
elastic solid mechanics, in which the primal and the sensitivity problem are both
solved by a lattice Boltzmann scheme. `periodicPlateOptiParam2d` solves the same
inverse problem with the adjoint LBM, which makes the two cases a direct check of
the generated adjoint collision kernel against f-AD.

The benchmark and its results are described in
[@grafenBenchmarkCasesGradientbased2026].

#### Setup

The domain is the unit square $\Omega = [0,1]^2$ with periodic boundaries,
discretized by $N_x$ nodes per Cartesian direction. The primal problem is the
quasistationary linear elasticity case of `structuralmechanics/linearElasticity/quasistationary/periodicPlate`,
solved with the MRT scheme of [@boolakee:23a] on a `D2Q8` descriptor in its
OpenLB implementation [@kaiser:25]. Following
that reference a manufactured steady-state displacement is prescribed,

$$
\symbf{u}^*(\symbf{x}) = \begin{pmatrix}
  \delta_1 \cos(2\pi x_1) \sin(2\pi x_2) \\
  \delta_2 \sin(2\pi x_1) \cos(2\pi x_2)
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \delta_1 = 9 \cdot 10^{-4}, \quad \delta_2 = 7 \cdot 10^{-4},
$$

with $E = 0.11$ and $\nu = 0.8$. Inserting $\symbf{u}^*$ into the steady
Navier--Cauchy equation gives the body force that produces it,

$$
\symbf{F}^* = 4\pi^2 \begin{pmatrix}
  \big[K(\delta_1+\delta_2) + 2\mu\delta_1\big]\cos(2\pi x_1)\sin(2\pi x_2) \\
  \big[K(\delta_1+\delta_2) + 2\mu\delta_2\big]\sin(2\pi x_1)\cos(2\pi x_2)
\end{pmatrix},
$$

where $K$ and $\mu$ are the two-dimensional bulk and shear modulus. This force has
vanishing mean, so a steady state exists on the periodic domain, and the residual
rigid translation is fixed by the zero initial condition $\symbf{u}(\symbf{x}, t=0) = \symbf{0}$
imposed at the beginning of every optimization step.

#### Inverse problem

The control is the pair of scalars that scales the two components of $\symbf{F}^*$ at
the lattice nodes,

$$
\symbf{F}(\symbf{x}_n, \symbf{\alpha}) = \symbf{\alpha} \circ \symbf{F}^*(\symbf{x}_n)
  = \begin{pmatrix} \alpha_1 F^*_1(\symbf{x}_n) \\ \alpha_2 F^*_2(\symbf{x}_n) \end{pmatrix},
$$

so the reference control is $\symbf{\alpha}^* = (1, 1)^{\mathsf{T}}$ by construction.
The objective measures the deviation from the sampled manufactured displacement
over the whole lattice,

$$
J(\symbf{\alpha}) = \tfrac{1}{2} \big\| \symbf{u}(\symbf{\alpha}) - \symbf{u}^* \big\|^2_{L^2(\Omega_{\Delta x})} ,
$$

and is minimized with L-BFGS. The control space is two-dimensional and independent
of the resolution, so the same problem is posed on every grid and only the discrete
solution operator changes with $N_x$.

#### Implementation

`case.h` defines `MyCase` as a `Case<names::NavierCauchy, Lattice<double, D2Q8<...>>>`
and derives the differentiated case by `MyCase::exchange_value_t<ADf>`. Both are
handed to an `OptiCaseADf<Controlled, MyCase, Derivatives, MyADfCase, Reference, MyCase>`,
which evaluates the objective on the `Controlled` case and obtains
$\mathrm{d}J/\mathrm{d}\symbf{\alpha}$ from the `ADf`-typed copy. Because the control has
only two entries, one tangent direction per entry is enough and f-AD is cheap here.
The manufactured displacement, stress and force are implemented in
`analyticalSolution.h`.

#### Files

```
periodicPlateOptiAD2d/
├── periodicPlateOptiAD2d.cpp  main(): default parameters, optimizer settings, run
├── case.h                     Case and ADf-typed case, geometry, lattice, objective
├── analyticalSolution.h       manufactured displacement, stress and body force
└── Makefile
```

This example ships no case file: the whole study is driven from the command line.
Every parameter set in the `.cpp` can be overridden there (`--RESOLUTION 20`), and
a `--case-file` of the same shape as the ones in `periodicPlateOpti2d` would work
if a study needs its settings pinned. The precedence is
`set<>()` < case file < command line.

Two defaults differ from the values the benchmark uses and are therefore passed on
the command line: `PHYS_MAX_T` is `30` in the source against $T_{max} = 100$ in the
study, and `ANALYTICAL_REFERENCE` is `false`, which compares against a simulated
rather than the manufactured reference.

#### Parameters

All of the following are set in `periodicPlateOptiAD2d.cpp` and can be overridden
from a case file or the command line. Vector-valued entries are passed in
brackets, `--INITIAL_CONTROL "[-1 -1]"`.

##### Geometry and discretization

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RESOLUTION` | int | `40` | nodes per Cartesian direction, $N_x$; the lattice holds $N_x^2$ nodes |
| `DOMAIN_EXTENT` | double[2] | `{1.0, 1.0}` | physical size of the periodic square |
| `ORIGIN` | double[2] | `{0.0, 0.0}` | lower-left corner of the domain |
| `PHYS_CHAR_LENGTH` | double | `1.0` | characteristic length of the unit converter |
| `PHYS_DELTA_X` | double | derived | $\Delta x =$ `DOMAIN_EXTENT[0] / RESOLUTION` |
| `PHYS_DELTA_T` | double | derived | $\Delta t = \Delta x^2$, the diffusive scaling of the pseudo-time |
| `PHYS_CHAR_DISPLACEMENT` | double | derived | displacement scale of the converter, set to $\Delta x$ |

The three derived values are computed in `main()` from `DOMAIN_EXTENT` and
`RESOLUTION` once the parameter block has been read, so overriding `RESOLUTION`
on the command line updates them too.

##### Material

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SOLID_CASE` | string | `"continua"` | dimensional reduction of the constitutive law; accepts `continua`, `planeStress`, `planeStrain` and `standard` |
| `YOUNGS_MODULUS` | double | `0.11` | $E$ of the simulated material |
| `POISSON_RATIO` | double | `0.8` | $\nu$; in 2D the admissible range is $-1 < \nu < 1$ |
| `PHYS_DENSITY` | double | `1` | $\rho$ |
| `DAMPING_FACTOR` | double | `1.0` | $\kappa$ of the damped pseudo-time scheme; also sets the stress conversion factor $\kappa \Delta x^2 / \Delta t$ |

##### Pseudo-time stepping and convergence

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHYS_MAX_T` | double | `30` | pseudo-time budget; the step cap is `PHYS_MAX_T`$/\Delta t = $ `PHYS_MAX_T`$\cdot N_x^2$. The benchmark uses `100` |
| `CONVERGENCE_PRECISION` | double | `1e-7` | relative tolerance of the steady-state check; `0` disables the check and runs the full budget |
| `CONV_ITER` | double | `10` | window length of the `ValueTracer` that watches the monitored value |
| `CONV_VALUE` | double | `1` | slot the case writes the monitored value into (the mean squared displacement); not a user knob |

There is no adjoint tolerance here: the sensitivity comes from the `ADf`-typed
copy of the primal solve, which converges together with it rather than in a
second solve.

##### Inverse problem and control

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `INITIAL_CONTROL` | double[2] | `{0, 0}` | $\symbf{\alpha}^{(0)}$, the two scalars scaling the components of $\symbf{F}^*$; the benchmark starts from `[-1 -1]` |
| `ANALYTICAL_REFERENCE` | bool | `false` | `true` compares against the sampled manufactured displacement, `false` against a reference obtained from a simulation; the benchmark uses `1` |

##### Output

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VTK_ENABLED` | bool | `true` | write the displacement, stress and control fields to VTK |
| `LATTICE_VTK_ITER_T` | int | `1000` | pseudo-time steps between VTK writes |
| `LATTICE_LOG_ITER_T` | int | `1000` | pseudo-time steps between console log lines; a very large value silences the log |

##### Optimizer

Held in a separate `OptimizerParametersD` in `main()` rather than in the case
parameters, and namespaced by optimizer component.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `optimizer::EPS` | double | `1e-10` | termination tolerance on the gradient norm |
| `optimizer::MAX_OPTIMIZATION_STEPS` | int | `50` | cap on the number of optimization steps |
| `optimizer::VERBOSE` | bool | `true` | per-step optimizer log |
| `linesearch::MAX_STEP_ATTEMPTS` | int | `100` | cap on line-search refinements within one step |

Unlike `periodicPlateOptiParam2d`, this case leaves `LBFGS::HISTORY_SIZE` and
`linesearch::STEP_CONDITION` at their library defaults.

#### Running the case

This example has a single mode: there is no `FORWARD_ONLY` switch and no gradient
comparison, so every run solves the inverse problem.

The defaults in `periodicPlateOptiAD2d.cpp` run $N_x = 40$ from
$\symbf{\alpha}^{(0)} = (0,0)^{\mathsf{T}}$. Parameters can be overridden on the command
line or through a case file. The resolution study of the benchmark uses

```sh
mpirun -np 2 ./periodicPlateOptiAD2d --RESOLUTION 20 --INITIAL_CONTROL "[-1 -1]" \
  --ANALYTICAL_REFERENCE 1 --CONVERGENCE_PRECISION 1e-7 --PHYS_MAX_T 100 --VTK_ENABLED 0
```

repeated for $N_x \in \{10, 20, 40, 80\}$. The optimization history is written to
`tmp/gnuplotData/data/optiLog.dat`, one row per step, holding the control, the
objective, the gradient norm and the relative control error.

#### Results

The results of this benchmark are reported and discussed in
[@grafenBenchmarkCasesGradientbased2026]: the evolution of the objective, of the
gradient norm and of the relative control error over the resolutions and over
four different initial controls, together with the agreement between the f-AD
gradient computed here and the ALBM gradient of `periodicPlateOptiParam2d`.
